existing_entries.title: Two-component architecture: one shared reporter, ten interchangeable sensing modules
existing_entries.value:
Insect odorant receptors are **not GPCRs**. A tuning receptor and the obligate co-receptor Orco
assemble into a heteromeric **ligand-gated cation channel**; odorant binding opens the pore
directly, with no second messenger in between. Orco also chaperones the tuning receptor to the
plasma membrane — without it the tuning receptor stays in the ER.

Two consequences shape this collection:

1. **The read-out can be shared.** Every tuning receptor needs the same Orco, and the channel
   conducts Ca²⁺, so one calcium-indicator–Orco fusion serves as the read-out for all of them. That
   is `BBa_26E11Z80`, the only part in the collection carrying a reporter.
2. **Specificity is the only interchangeable layer.** The ten sensing modules differ from each other
   in nothing but the tuning receptor CDS. Swapping one for another changes what the cell detects
   and leaves the read-out, the optics, the calculation and the controls untouched.

A working sensor is always **two co-transfected parts**: one sensing module plus `BBa_26E11Z80`.
Neither is a device alone.

### Collection-wide design decisions

| Decision | Applies to | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| **Codon-optimised for human expression** | all 11 receptor CDSs, incl. Orco | Zboray *et al.* (2023) used **wild-type** OR sequences and identified translation as a likely bottleneck, writing that "functional OR protein expression can be improved by codon optimization of OR genes instead of using wild type sequences". This collection takes that route; it is the largest deliberate difference from that study. |
| **EMCV IRES + mCherry** on every sensing module | the 10 modules | One transcript, two separate proteins. mCherry is translated cap-independently, so red fluorescence reports that the transcript reached the cytoplasm **even when the receptor is non-functional** — the case that is otherwise undiagnosable. A 2A peptide was rejected because it leaves a residual peptide on the receptor. |
| **GCCACC Kozak** on every ORF | all composites | strong mammalian initiation |
| **No promoter, no polyA** | all parts | portable coding parts; the host vector sets expression level and induction. Every part here needs a promoter and terminator from its host vector. |
| **Receptors supplied both as bare CDS and as a module** | 10 + 10 parts | the bare CDS (e.g. `BBa_26VGDFA1`) for teams assembling into their own context; the module (e.g. `BBa_26ZAGFK0`) as a ready bicistronic unit |

The geometry of the reporter fusion — why the indicator is at the **N**-terminus, why the linker is
the length it is — is intrinsic to `BBa_26E11Z80` and documented there. The inverted membrane
topology that forces it is documented on `BBa_26LWIKBQ` (DmOrco CDS).

### Where the sequences come from

Nothing here was cloned from an organism, evolved, or computationally designed. The eleven receptor
coding sequences are the **native *Drosophila melanogaster* protein sequences back-translated with
human codon usage** and synthesised; each encodes a protein identical to its FlyBase reference.

| part | receptor | FlyBase gene | transcript | RefSeq protein | aa |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BBa_26LWIKBQ` | Orco | FBgn0037324 | FBtr0078794 | NP_524235 | 486 |
| `BBa_26VGDFA1` | Or7a | FBgn0030016 | FBtr0071186 | NP_511081 | 413 |
| `BBa_26HTXB02` | Or19a | FBgn0041626 | FBtr0070029 | NP_525013 | 387 |
| `BBa_26AIIWHV` | Or22a | FBgn0026398 | FBtr0077873 | NP_523453 | 397 |
| `BBa_26HJ1RUT` | Or35a | FBgn0028946 | FBtr0080781 | NP_723916 | 409 |
| `BBa_26UHN7NT` | Or42a | FBgn0033041 | FBtr0086052 | NP_523622 | 406 |
| `BBa_26OJ8HGO` | Or59b | FBgn0034865 | FBtr0072021 | NP_523822 | 398 |
| `BBa_26XXP4K7` | Or67a | FBgn0036009 | FBtr0076375 | NP_524005 | 407 |
| `BBa_26ACVV3R` | Or67b | FBgn0036019 | FBtr0076420 | NP_524007 | 421 |
| `BBa_26DVVZIA` | Or85b | FBgn0037590 | FBtr0081900 | NP_524279 | 390 |
| `BBa_26DG1NPK` | Or98a | FBgn0039551 | FBtr0085226 | NP_524536 | 397 |

The non-receptor components:

| part | origin |
|---|---|
| `BBa_26QHYP02` GCaMP6f | derived from Addgene **#40755**; indicator described by Chen *et al.* (2013) |
| `BBa_26E21OEQ` (GGGGS)₃ linker | fully synthetic; the three repeats use **diversified synonymous codons** so the DNA carries no tandem repeat, which is a common cause of synthesis failure and polymerase slippage |
| `BBa_262WP16P` RSET leader | the N-terminal leader of the **pRSET** vector series (Invitrogen) |
| EMCV IRES (inside the 10 modules) | encephalomyocarditis virus internal ribosome entry site, wild-type |
| mCherry (inside the 10 modules) | Shaner *et al.* (2004) |

All constructs were **synthesised by GenScript** and delivered in an IP-free version of the
pcDNA3.1(+) backbone.

### The odorant panel that was actually tested, and what was known about it

Six compounds plus the Orco agonist were tested. Two of the six were lost to the gain
fault (collection *Experiment* entry). This is what the literature says about each of them **for the
receptors in this collection** — responses reported for receptors not in this collection are not
relevant and are excluded:

| compound | class | published response on a receptor in **this** collection |
|---|---|---|
| **VUAA1**, 50 µM | synthetic Orco agonist | activates every Orco-containing line; the positive control for the whole platform (Jones *et al.* 2011) |
| **isopentyl acetate** *(lost to gain fault)* | ester | **Or98a, 0.31** VUAA1-normalised at 100 µM — the strongest published match in the panel |
| **2-heptanone** | methyl ketone | **Or85b, 0.55** at 100 µM — Or85b's reference ligand, EC₅₀ **68.9 µM**; also Or98a 0.11 |
| **3-octanol** | secondary alcohol | Or98a, 0.13 at 100 µM |
| **benzaldehyde** | aromatic aldehyde | **none.** Reported for Or49b (0.23) and Or10a (0.17), neither of which is in this collection |
| **ethyl propionate** *(lost to gain fault)* | ester | **none reported** |
| **valeric acid** | carboxylic acid | **none reported.** No carboxylic acid appears anywhere in the responsive ligand set of Zboray *et al.* (2023), for any of their seven lines |

Three consequences follow, and all three are uncomfortable:

1. **Only two of the eleven receptors in this collection had any published reason to respond to this
   panel** — Or85b and Or98a. For the other nine the panel was a blind screen.
2. **The one compound with the strongest published match, isopentyl acetate on Or98a, is one of the
   two that the gain fault destroyed.** The loss was not two arbitrary compounds; it was the
   best-predicted odorant × receptor combination on the plate.
3. **The panel was dosed by a dilution factor inherited from fly work, and the resulting molar
   concentrations are unknown.** The supplied stock's concentration was never recorded, so none of
   these published EC₅₀ values can be compared against what was actually delivered. See the
   *Experiment* entry.

The reasoning that led to this particular set of six is not recorded in this documentation; a future
team should choose by EC₅₀ and by the receptors actually in hand.

### Parts in this collection

**Read-out (1)** — `BBa_26E11Z80` GCaMP6f-(GGGGS)₃-DmOrco, 2,862 bp

**Sensing modules (10)**, all `<OR>-IRES-mCherry` —
`BBa_26ZAGFK0` Or7a · `BBa_2629NIWH` Or19a · `BBa_26WOX4B1` Or22a · `BBa_26LLF3LM` Or35a ·
`BBa_26Q1Q094` Or42a · `BBa_26Y7CI2H` Or59b · `BBa_265G8CE1` Or67a · `BBa_269VSDDR` Or67b ·
`BBa_26K1TU11` Or85b · `BBa_26TZLBMJ` Or98a

**Tuning receptor CDSs (10)** —
`BBa_26VGDFA1` Or7a · `BBa_26HTXB02` Or19a · `BBa_26AIIWHV` Or22a · `BBa_26HJ1RUT` Or35a ·
`BBa_26UHN7NT` Or42a · `BBa_26OJ8HGO` Or59b · `BBa_26XXP4K7` Or67a · `BBa_26ACVV3R` Or67b ·
`BBa_26DVVZIA` Or85b · `BBa_26DG1NPK` Or98a

**Components of the read-out fusion (4)** —
`BBa_26LWIKBQ` DmOrco CDS · `BBa_26QHYP02` GCaMP6f · `BBa_26E21OEQ` (GGGGS)₃ linker ·
`BBa_262WP16P` RSET leader

### References

1. Zboray K, Mohamed Mahmoud M, Pató A, *et al.* Stable cell lines expressing *Drosophila* odorant receptors for the detection of plant pathogen-related volatile organic compounds. *Sci Rep* **13**, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4
2. Jones PL, Pask GM, Rinker DC, Zwiebel LJ. Functional agonism of insect odorant receptor ion channels. *PNAS* **108**, 8821–8825 (2011).
3. Chen T-W, Wardill TJ, Sun Y, *et al.* Ultrasensitive fluorescent proteins for imaging neuronal activity. *Nature* **499**, 295–300 (2013).
4. Shaner NC, Campbell RE, Steinbach PA, *et al.* Improved monomeric red, orange and yellow fluorescent proteins derived from *Discosoma* sp. red fluorescent protein. *Nat Biotechnol* **22**, 1567–1572 (2004).
5. FlyBase — https://flybase.org/ (accessions in the table above)
6. DoOR 2.0 — Database of Odorant Responses. http://neuro.uni-konstanz.de/DoOR/

existing_entries.title: Plate-reader calcium assay: conditions, two-round addition, calculation, gain QC
existing_entries.value:
Every number in this collection comes from **one experiment, run on 2026-10-10**: a single 96-well
plate, one well per condition.

### Chassis and transfection

| | |
|---|---|
| Cells | HEK293, uncoated 96-well black-wall clear-bottom plate (GREINER 96 F-BOTTOM) |
| Transfection | **transient co-transfection** of one sensing module + `BBa_26E11Z80` |
| On-plate controls | column 11 = `BBa_26E11Z80` alone (no tuning receptor); column 12 = **untransfected** HEK293 |

### Reader

| | |
|---|---|
| Instrument | BMG LABTECH **CLARIOstar Plus**, SMART Control / MARS |
| Mode | fluorescence intensity, plate mode, kinetic, **bottom optic** |
| Optics | Ex **482-16** / Dichroic **LP 504** / Em **530-40** |
| Focal height | **−4.1 mm** |
| Flashes per well per cycle | 20 |
| Settling time | 0.5 s |
| Cycle time | **12 s** (instrument minimum for this layout: 10 s) |
| Enhanced dynamic range | **off**; full scale 260,000 RFU |
| Temperature control | **off** (ambient) |
| Shaking | none |

### Assay buffer

140 mM NaCl · 5 mM KCl · **2 mM CaCl₂** · 1 mM MgCl₂ · 5 mM HEPES-Na · 20 mM glucose, pH 7.3.
Recipe after Zboray *et al.* (2023). The Ca²⁺ is load-bearing: that study abolished the Orco-agonist response in
Ca²⁺-free buffer and in Ca²⁺-free buffer with EGTA, which is what establishes that the fluorescence
rise reports **extracellular** Ca²⁺ entering through the channel.

### The two-round addition — and why it matters more than it looks

| step | action | read | cycles | volume in well |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | plate the cells in assay buffer | **F0a** — baseline | 5 | 100 µL |
| 2 | **+ 50 µL plain assay buffer** — *round 1, the vehicle control* | **blank** | 15 | 150 µL |
| 3 | — | **F0b** — new baseline | 5 | 150 µL |
| 4 | **+ 50 µL compound at 4× final** — *round 2, the ligand* | **test** | 15 | 200 µL |

Volume goes 100 → 150 → 200 µL; compounds are added at 4× so they end at 1× in 200 µL.
VUAA1: 200 µM in the added 50 µL → **50 µM final**.

### Odorant concentrations are not known — the most serious limitation of this experiment

The odorants were supplied as aqueous solutions by another laboratory, whose stated practice was to
dilute those solutions **10,000-fold** for *Drosophila* odorant testing. That same 10,000-fold
dilution was applied here. **The concentration of the supplied solutions was not recorded, so the
molar concentration of every odorant in the well is unknown and cannot be reconstructed.**

Two consequences, both of which limit what any part page in this collection may claim:

1. **No odorant result can be placed on a dose axis.** Nothing in this collection may be described
   as under- or over-dosed, and no value may be compared against a published EC₅₀. Where an earlier
   draft of this documentation explained a null result by saying the dose was below the EC₅₀, that
   explanation was unfounded and has been removed.
2. **A dilution factor does not transfer between a fly assay and a cell assay.** In *Drosophila*
   work an odorant is diluted in oil or water and the animal is exposed to the **headspace above the
   liquid** — the stimulus is the vapour, which is orders of magnitude more dilute than the liquid
   it evaporated from. Here the cells sit **in the liquid** and meet the liquid concentration
   directly. The same "1:10,000" therefore denotes two different stimuli, and the convention was
   carried across formats without that being noticed.

**What a repeat requires before anything else:** the supplied stock's concentration in g/L or mol/L,
or odorants weighed out and dissolved to a known molarity, so that each receptor can be dosed in µM
around its own published EC₅₀.

Every well therefore carries **its own vehicle control in the same well** — round 1 is an identical
50 µL addition and plate transfer with no ligand. That is the strength of the design and also its
weakness: because the reported value is round 2 minus round 1, **anything that happens to the well
during round 1 is subtracted out of round 2 with the opposite sign.** A well that loses baseline
fluorescence in round 1 produces a large positive ΔF_corr with no ligand effect whatsoever. This
caught three wells on this plate; see the *Characterisation* entry.

**Pipetting:** an 8-channel pipette against a 12-column plate means two passes — columns 1–8, then
9–12, in the same fixed order every time. The resulting time offset is identical in both rounds and
cancels in the correction.

### Calculation

| quantity | definition |
|---|---|
| **F0** | mean of the 5 baseline cycles of that round |
| **F_MAX** | maximum of the 3-cycle moving average — a single-point maximum is positively biased |
| **ΔF_blank** | ( F_MAX(round 1) − F0a ) / F0a |
| **ΔF_test** | ( F_MAX(round 2) − F0b ) / F0b |
| **ΔF_corr** | ΔF_test − ΔF_blank |
| **ΔF_norm** | ΔF_corr ÷ ΔF_corr(VUAA1, same column) — reported but unusable, see *Discussion* |

Every part page reports **all three** of ΔF_blank, ΔF_test and ΔF_corr, never ΔF_corr alone.

### Gain QC — why two compounds are missing from every table

Detector gain on this instrument is **not stored in the protocol**; it is set in the Start
Measurement dialog and is lost whenever the protocol is edited. It was not held constant across all
32 reads of this session.

ΔF is a ratio **within one well**, so a different gain in a different row is harmless. But the `F0`
read and the response read it is divided by **must share a gain**. To test that without assuming it,
the untransfected wells (column 12), which should not respond to anything, were used as an absolute
yardstick:

| row | compound | median col-12 F0a | round 1 / F0a | round 2 / F0b | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | VUAA1 | 1610 | 0.998 | 0.951 | valid |
| **B** | **ethyl propionate** | 1408 | **1.348** | **1.366** | **discarded** — both pairs mismatched |
| **C** | **isopentyl acetate** | 551 | **3.117** | 1.017 | **discarded** — round 1 pair mismatched |
| D | 3-octanol | 2182 | 0.999 | 1.034 | valid |
| E | benzaldehyde | 1946 | 1.002 | 1.049 | valid |
| F | 2-heptanone | 2437 | 1.012 | 1.055 | valid |
| G | valeric acid | 1731 | 1.011 | 1.074 | valid |
| H | Control (buffer) | 18726 | 0.950 | 0.951 | valid (internally consistent; absolute gain ~10× the others, which does not affect a within-well ratio) |

**Two of eight compounds — ethyl propionate and isopentyl acetate — produced no usable data at all.**
This was the largest single loss in the experiment.

**Fix for anyone repeating this:** run gain adjustment once, **write the number down**, then type
that value manually into every subsequent read and leave `Gain Adjustment` unchecked for the rest of
the session.

### References

1. Zboray K, Mohamed Mahmoud M, Pató A, *et al.* Stable cell lines expressing *Drosophila* odorant receptors for the detection of plant pathogen-related volatile organic compounds. *Sci Rep* **13**, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4
2. BMG LABTECH SMART Control Software Manual Part II (0430F0049A, 2022-09-09) — §3.4 Data Output, §6.5 Plate Identification, §6.6 Sample IDs.

existing_entries.title: Four measured acceptance criteria, and the buffer-only well that satisfies three
existing_entries.value:
Before any per-part number can be read, two things had to be established: that the read-out works,
and how large a signal this plate produces **with nothing added**.

### 1. The read-out works

`BBa_26E11Z80` with no tuning receptor responded to 50 µM VUAA1 (ΔF\_corr +0.2148, ligand round
+0.1186, gradual) while untransfected cells in the same row gave +0.0041. The full data, kinetics,
controls and caveats are intrinsic to that part and are documented on `BBa_26E11Z80`.

### 2. Four acceptance criteria, all measured — none assumed

The untransfected wells (column 12: same additions, same handling, no receptor, every valid row)
give the noise of each quantity directly. Taking 3 SD of each:

| # | criterion                         | bound         | measured from                                                                                                                                                                                                         |               |                                                                     |
| - | --------------------------------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1 | ΔF\_corr ≥ **0.134**              | 3 × SD 0.0448 | untransfected ΔF\_corr, n \= 6                                                                                                                                                                                        |               |                                                                     |
| 2 | ΔF\_test ≥ **0.089**              | 3 × SD 0.0296 | untransfected ΔF\_test, n \= 6 — *the ligand round must itself rise*                                                                                                                                                  |               |                                                                     |
| 3 |                                   | ΔF\_blank     | ≤ **0.060**                                                                                                                                                                                                           | 3 × SD 0.0200 | untransfected ΔF\_blank, n \= 6 — *the vehicle round must be quiet* |
| 4 | frac\_at\_first\_read \< **0.60** | —             | shape: the fraction of the total rise already present at the first post-addition cycle. Near 1.0 means the change was complete before the plate finished re-inserting — an optical or physical step, not Ca²⁺ influx. |               |                                                                     |

**Criterion 3 is the one that is easy to forget and it changed several readings on this plate.**
Because ΔF\_corr \= round 2 − round 1, a well that *loses* baseline in round 1 reports a large
positive ΔF\_corr with no ligand effect at all. Three wells did exactly that.

### 3. Every condition over 0.134, decomposed

| compound                  | cell line | ΔF\_blank  | ΔF\_test   | ΔF\_corr   | frac | criteria failed                                  |
| ------------------------- | --------- | ---------- | ---------- | ---------- | ---- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| **Control (buffer only)** | **Or35a** | −0.096     | **+0.353** | **+0.449** | 0.16 | 3 only                                           |
| Control (buffer only)     | Or42a     | **−0.301** | +0.014     | +0.315     | —    | 2 and 3 — 95 % of the value is the vehicle round |
| valeric acid              | Or35a     | −0.117     | +0.177     | +0.295     | 0.87 | 3 and 4                                          |
| **valeric acid**          | **Or85b** | −0.013     | +0.204     | +0.217     | 0.59 | **none**                                         |
| VUAA1 50 µM               | ORCO only | −0.096     | +0.119     | +0.215     | 0.06 | 3 only                                           |
| 2-heptanone               | ORCO only | +0.025     | +0.210     | +0.186     | 0.83 | 4                                                |
| 2-heptanone               | Or7a      | **−0.164** | +0.020     | +0.184     | —    | 2 and 3 — 89 % of the value is the vehicle round |
| valeric acid              | ORCO only | +0.040     | +0.197     | +0.158     | 0.77 | 4                                                |
| benzaldehyde              | ORCO only | +0.027     | +0.165     | +0.138     | 0.90 | 4                                                |
| **VUAA1 50 µM**           | **Or35a** | +0.040     | +0.178     | +0.137     | 0.49 | **none**                                         |

### 4. The result that sets the ceiling on everything else

Row H received **plain assay buffer in both rounds**. Every well in it should read zero. The Or35a
well instead rose **+0.353 in round 2**, gradually, peaking at 96 s, giving ΔF\_corr **+0.449** — the
largest value on the plate, from a well that never saw a ligand. It satisfies criteria 1, 2 and 4
and fails only 3, and it fails 3 only narrowly (−0.096 against a −0.060 bound).

![Two line charts of fluorescence change over time for all 12 columns of the buffer-only row. In round 2, with only assay buffer added, the Or35a trace rises above the 0.134 threshold to +0.35; in round 1 the Or42a trace sits 30 % below its own baseline. The other ten columns stay within ±0.1.](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/9dfa1d46-443b-491e-b31d-f454c65f55ec/7fd45191845ab3fe49775a76fe355123055b9f553f63860d4e9f01b4aa63e0f9.avif "Buffer-only row, both rounds — the plate’s false positives")

*Row H, all 12 columns, both rounds, raw fluorescence as (F − F₀)/F₀ against time. Left: round 1.
Right: round 2 — also plain buffer. Or35a (blue) rises past the threshold in round 2 with no ligand
present. Or42a (orange) does the opposite: it loses 30 % of its baseline at the round-1 addition and
never recovers, which the subtraction then converts into a spurious +0.315. The ten grey traces are
the other columns, all within ±0.1.*

**This is the most important single result on the plate.** A buffer-only well produced a larger,
better-shaped signal than any odorant did. At n \= 1, the four criteria are **necessary but not
sufficient**, and no odorant response on this plate is distinguishable from the plate's own noise,
however good it looks. Two conditions pass all four criteria — valeric acid × Or85b (+0.217) and
VUAA1 × Or35a (+0.137) — and both are smaller than +0.449. They are documented on their part pages
as **conditions to repeat, not as hits**.

existing_entries.title: What this plate establishes, what it does not, and the seven changes the next run needs
existing_entries.value:
### Established

**One thing.** The reporter fusion `BBa_26E11Z80` is expressed, reaches the plasma membrane, and
gates Ca²⁺ in response to an Orco agonist, in transiently transfected HEK293. That makes the
platform real. The caveats on the magnitude are on that part's page.

### Not established

**No odorant response was demonstrated for any of the ten tuning receptors.** Not "the receptors do
not work" — the experiment could not have detected it if they did. Four reasons, each sufficient
alone:

**1. Expression, not ligand choice, is the limiting factor.** VUAA1 acts on **Orco** and bypasses
the tuning receptor, so all eleven Orco-containing columns should have responded. Only two did:
ORCO-only (+0.215) and Or35a (+0.137). **Nine of eleven Orco-containing wells failed their own
positive control.** Whatever the tuning receptors would have done to an odorant, this plate was not
in a state to see it. Zboray *et al.* (2023) reported the same pattern in several of their lines and attributed it to
translation and ER-export bottlenecks.

**2. The delivered dose is unknown, so no null result can be interpreted.** The odorants came as
stock solutions of unrecorded concentration, diluted 10,000-fold by a convention borrowed from
*Drosophila* experiments in which the animal samples the vapour rather than the liquid (see the
*Experiment* entry). Against that, Zboray *et al.* (2023) report EC₅₀ = 68.9 µM for 2-heptanone on Or85b and reach a
VUAA1-normalised 0.55 only at 100 µM, and Or98a's reference ligand (6-methyl-5-hepten-2-one,
EC₅₀ 2.06 µM) was not on the plate at all. Whether this experiment landed above, below or near those
values cannot be determined from the records.

**3. The vehicle round is not inert, and the correction amplifies that.** Three wells moved more
than ±0.060 during round 1; in two of them the vehicle round supplied 89 % and 95 % of the reported
ΔF_corr. Mechanically this looks like cell loss or a bubble at the moment of addition — consistent
with an uncoated plate and a 2.5 h session — not like receptor behaviour.

**4. The odorant working solutions appear to differ physically from the assay buffer.** The
ORCO-only column has no tuning receptor and no odorant specificity. It nevertheless moved in **every**
odorant row and not in the buffer row, and all three of those movements are step-shaped
(frac 0.77–0.90):

| row | ORCO-only ΔF_test | frac |
|---|---|---|
| VUAA1 | +0.119 | 0.06 |
| 3-octanol | +0.121 | — |

Add the buffer-only well that reached +0.449 (see *Characterisation*), and the honest summary is:

specificity.**

ΔF_norm (ΔF_corr ÷ the same column's VUAA1 value) is in the dataset but is **not usable for this
plate**: nine of eleven VUAA1 denominators are at or below the noise floor, so the quotient is a
ratio of two noise values. It becomes meaningful only once every column passes its VUAA1 control.

1. **Fix the gain manually.** Adjust once, record the value, type it in for every read, leave
   `Gain Adjustment` unchecked. This cost two of eight compounds.

   session. This is the most likely source of both the 0.045 noise floor and the three round-1
   baseline collapses.

   in it. This directly tests reason 4. If the ORCO-only column steps in that row too, the
   odorant-row signals are solution artefacts and the question is settled.

   instead of eight. This session ran 2.5 h.

existing_entries.value:
This module supplies one thing to the platform: **the ligand specificity of Or19a**. The pore, the
trafficking and the read-out all come from `BBa_26E11Z80`; the collection's *Design* entry covers
that split and the collection-wide choices (codon optimisation, the IRES-mCherry arrangement, the
Kozak, the absence of a promoter).

### Prior art for this receptor

Cloned from *D. melanogaster* Canton S and expressed as a stable HEK293 line by Zboray *et al.* (2023), where it was
**one of the four non-responsive lines** — again despite strong DoOR predictions. Wild-type sequence
in that study; codon-optimised here.

### What the odorant panel offered this receptor

**None of the six compounds tested has a published response for this receptor.** Zboray *et al.* (2023) either
did not test it or obtained no response, and the compounds that did respond in that study did so on
receptors that are not in this collection. Whether DoOR 2.0 predicts a response to any of the six is
**[TO FILL: check DoOR 2.0 for 3-octanol, benzaldehyde, 2-heptanone, valeric acid, isopentyl
acetate, ethyl propionate]**. The panel was, for this receptor, a blind screen.

The panel as a whole, and why it is weaker than it should be, is in the collection's *Design* entry.

The receptor coding sequence is `BBa_26HTXB02` — FlyBase accession, protein length and synthesis route are on
that part's page. The module adds an EMCV IRES and mCherry (Shaner *et al.* 2004) around it; the
whole construct was synthesised by GenScript in an IP-free pcDNA3.1(+) backbone.

existing_entries.title: An inert epitope handle for a fusion that has no other tag — and the experiment it exists for
existing_entries.value:
### What it is for

The reporter fusion in this collection carries no fluorescent tag on the protein (GCaMP6f is dim
until Ca²⁺ arrives) and no epitope tag. When such a construct gives no calcium response, the first
question is **"was the protein made at all?"** — and without a handle that question is unanswerable.

This leader makes it answerable by Western blot or immunostaining, via anti-His or anti-Xpress.

### Why it can be left in during functional assays

In mammalian cells this leader is **functionally inert**: it is not a signal peptide, it targets the
protein nowhere, and it is not cleaved. The enterokinase site allows removal if a tag-free protein is
ever wanted, but nothing in this collection requires that.

### Placement

N-terminal to GCaMP6f, i.e. at the **cytoplasmic** end of the fusion (Orco's N-terminus is
intracellular — see `BBa_26LWIKBQ`), where it cannot interfere with membrane insertion.

### Source

The N-terminal leader of the **pRSET** vector series (Invitrogen / Thermo Fisher). Synthetic as
supplied here; no source organism. It carries no sequence of our own design.

### Characterisation status, stated plainly

- **Evidence it does no harm:** the fusion carrying it is functional — `BBa_26E11Z80`, ΔF_corr
  +0.2148 and a gradual +0.1186 ligand round to 50 µM VUAA1 — so the leader does not prevent
  folding, trafficking or channel function.
- **It has never been used for its actual purpose.** No anti-His or anti-Xpress blot has been run on
  any construct in this collection, so there is no blot image on this page.

That omission matters: nine of eleven Orco-containing wells failed their VUAA1 positive
control and we cannot currently say whether the protein was absent, mislocalised, or present and
inactive. **This blot is the single most informative next experiment in the project**, it needs no
plate reader, and this part is what makes it possible.

### Reference

1. Zboray K, Mohamed Mahmoud M, Pató A, *et al.* Stable cell lines expressing *Drosophila* odorant receptors for the detection of plant pathogen-related volatile organic compounds. *Sci Rep* **13**, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4

existing_entries.title: Fusion geometry: why the indicator is N-terminal and why the linker was lengthened
existing_entries.value:
The collection's *Design* entry covers why there is a single shared reporter at all. This entry
covers the two decisions specific to **this molecule**.

### 1. GCaMP6f at the N-terminus

Orco has **inverted membrane topology** relative to a GPCR: its N-terminus is **intracellular**
(documented on `BBa_26LWIKBQ`). GCaMP6f must face the cytoplasm, because the Ca²⁺ it reports enters
from outside and is bound on the inner face. In Orco it is the N-terminus that is on that side. A
C-terminal fusion would put the indicator extracellularly, where there is no Ca²⁺ transient to
report and where the 2 mM bulk Ca²⁺ of the assay buffer would saturate it.

Tethering the indicator to the channel also puts it at the mouth of the pore it reports on rather
than in the bulk cytosol, and fixes the reporter-to-channel ratio at 1:1 by construction — a single
transcription unit cannot deliver them in any other proportion.

### 2. (GGGGS)₃ — 15 aa, longer than the published version

| | linker | length |
|---|---|---|
| Zboray *et al.* (2023) | Gly₂SerGly₃SerGly | 8 aa |
| this part | **(GGGGS)₃** | **15 aa** |

GCaMP6f is a ~50 kDa three-module protein (M13 peptide — circularly permuted EGFP — calmodulin)
whose signal depends on a conformational change across all three. Orco is a 7-TM membrane protein
that has to insert and oligomerise. 8 aa is enough to join them; 15 aa was chosen so neither folding
process constrains the other, at the cost of a slightly larger diffusion distance between pore and
sensor. **This is the one deliberate structural departure from the published construct**, and the
result below shows the fusion is functional with it. Whether 15 aa is better or worse than 8 aa is
untested — it would need both constructs side by side on one plate.

### 3. Supporting elements

- **RSET leader** (`BBa_262WP16P`) at the extreme N-terminus, i.e. the cytoplasmic end, where it
  cannot interfere with membrane insertion of Orco. Functionally inert in mammalian cells and the
  only epitope handle on the fusion.
- **GCCACC Kozak** for strong mammalian initiation.
- **No promoter or polyA**, so the host vector sets expression level and induction. Zboray *et al.* (2023) used a
  doxycycline-inducible promoter, partly because constitutive Orco expression has been reported to
  reduce long-term viability (see `BBa_26LWIKBQ`).

### Source

| element | origin |
|---|---|
| GCaMP6f | Addgene **#40755**; indicator described by Chen *et al.* (2013) |
| (GGGGS)₃ linker | fully synthetic, diversified synonymous codons |
| DmOrco | *D. melanogaster* Orco, FlyBase **FBgn0037324 / FBtr0078794**, RefSeq **NP_524235**, 486 aa — codon-optimised, protein identical to the reference |
| RSET leader | pRSET vector series (Invitrogen) |

Synthesised by GenScript as a single fragment and delivered in an IP-free version of the
pcDNA3.1(+) backbone. Nothing in this part was cloned from an organism or computationally designed.

### Reference

existing_entries.value:
Transiently transfected into HEK293 **with no tuning receptor**, 2026-10-10, one well per condition (well A11). Thresholds and conditions in the collection documentation (*Drosophila odorant receptor calcium-reporter platform*).

| compound                             | final conc. | ΔF\_blank | ΔF\_test | **ΔF\_corr**  | reading                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------- | --------- | -------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| VUAA1                                | 50 µM       | -0.0962   | +0.1186  | **+0.2148**   | over 0.134 but **fails criterion 3**: the vehicle round moved -0.096, outside the ±0.060 bound (45% of ΔF\_corr is that movement)       |
| 3-octanol                            | 1:10,000    | +0.0475   | +0.1205  | **+0.0730**   | below the 0.134 threshold — no response detected                                                                                        |
| benzaldehyde                         | 1:10,000    | +0.0267   | +0.1645  | **+0.1378**   | over 0.134 but **fails criterion 4**: step-shaped, frac 0.90                                                                            |
| 2-heptanone                          | 1:10,000    | +0.0248   | +0.2103  | **+0.1855**   | over 0.134 but **fails criterion 4**: step-shaped, frac 0.83                                                                            |
| valeric acid                         | 1:10,000    | +0.0395   | +0.1972  | **+0.1577**   | over 0.134 but **fails criterion 4**: step-shaped, frac 0.77                                                                            |
| Control (buffer only)                | —           | +0.0132   | -0.0035  | **-0.0167**   | below the 0.134 threshold — no response detected                                                                                        |
| ethyl propionate · isopentyl acetate | 1:10,000    | —         | —        | not evaluable | gain changed between the baseline and response reads in those two rows; both discarded by the QC in the collection's *Experiment* entry |

![Two line charts for the reporter-fusion-only well. Round 2 shows VUAA1 rising gradually to +0.12 over about 156 seconds while the three odorants step up instantly; round 1 shows the same well 10 % below baseline.](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/17f31275-4ad3-49b8-8730-47f2b1730623/202a22ee1903f5d9cd7818e1bed7f017f67106a57a3c259b6066dc899f0ce118.avif "BBa_26E11Z80 — both measurement rounds, six compounds")

*Both measurement rounds for this well, raw fluorescence expressed as (F − F₀)/F₀ against time after the 50 µL addition. **Left:** round 1, plain assay buffer — the vehicle control for every trace on the right. **Right:** round 2, the compound. The quoted ΔF\_corr is the right-hand peak minus the left-hand peak, so a trace that sags on the left inflates it.*

### The VUAA1 result, stated with both rounds

|                                               | value       |
| --------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| ΔF\_blank — round 1, 50 µL plain buffer       | **−0.0962** |
| ΔF\_test — round 2, 50 µL VUAA1 (50 µM final) | **+0.1186** |
| **ΔF\_corr**                                  | **+0.2148** |
| frac\_at\_first\_read                         | **0.06**    |
| time to peak                                  | 156 s       |

**The ligand round rose +0.1186**, above the 0.089 bound measured on this plate's untransfected
wells, and it rose *gradually*: only 6 % of the total was present at the first post-addition cycle,
the remaining 94 % developing over ~156 s. This is the slowest and cleanest kinetic on the plate and
the shape a ligand-gated channel filling a cell with Ca²⁺ produces; an optical or pipetting artefact
is complete before the first read (compare the plate's artefacts at frac 0.77–1.03 in the
collection's *Characterisation* entry).

**The vehicle round of this well was not quiet**, and that must be said plainly: it fell by 9.6 %,
outside the ±0.060 bound. The quoted ΔF\_corr of +0.2148 is therefore **inflated** — about 45 % of it
is the subtraction of that fall, not the VUAA1 response. This well fails acceptance criterion 3.
The honest single number for the response is **ΔF\_test = +0.119**; +0.215 should only ever be quoted
with the decomposition above beside it.

The fall itself is most likely photobleaching or cell loss in the brightest well on the row — this
is the well with the most reporter — rather than anything to do with VUAA1, which was not present
during round 1.

**What the raw trace shows, and why the result still stands.** In absolute RFU the well sits at
\~2470 during the first baseline, drops to ~2210 at the plain-buffer addition, and the VUAA1 round
then takes it back to ~2470. The rise is therefore a *recovery* to the pre-addition level rather
than an excursion above it, and that has to be said. What rules out spontaneous recovery is the
timing: the well stayed flat at ~2210 for the whole 180 s buffer round **and** the following 60 s
F0b baseline — about 290 s — and moved only when VUAA1 went in. A drift that recovers on its own
does not wait 290 s and then climb in step with an addition. The untransfected well in the same
row, same gain, neither fell nor rose.

![Raw fluorescence in RFU across the whole run for two wells. The reporter-fusion well drops from 2470 to 2210 when plain buffer is added, stays flat for about 290 seconds, then climbs back to 2470 after VUAA1. The untransfected well stays at 1600 throughout.](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/17f31275-4ad3-49b8-8730-47f2b1730623/d2252a3f59ed0e35cb34dec73fcf0ef4011ee0491330552776fd78c0ea67c56e.avif "VUAA1 opens the reporter fusion — raw trace, both additions")

*Raw RFU, 12 s cycles. Dashed line = addition of 50 µL VUAA1 at 200 µM (50 µM final). Blue: this
part alone, well A11. Orange: untransfected HEK293, same row, same additions, well A12.*

### Controls the result survives

| control                                                  | the alternative it rules out                                  | result                                                           |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Untransfected cells, same row, same additions, same gain | the plate, the optics, the liquid handling                    | ΔF\_corr **+0.0041**, ΔF\_test **+0.0098** — flat in both rounds |
| Same well, round 1: 50 µL plain buffer instead of VUAA1  | the mechanical act of adding 50 µL and re-inserting the plate | no rise (it fell — see the caveat above)                         |
| Same well, buffer-only row: both additions plain buffer  | upward drift of this well on its own                          | ΔF\_corr **−0.0167**, ΔF\_test **−0.0035**                       |
| Kinetic shape                                            | an instantaneous optical step                                 | gradual, frac 0.06, plateau ~156 s                              |

![Two line charts for the untransfected wells. Every trace in both rounds stays within ±0.05 of baseline — the experiment’s zero and the source of its detection thresholds.](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/17f31275-4ad3-49b8-8730-47f2b1730623/53b3c2831ea5c292dd61047d9ee7b6530ed09075ca0f0bf620f60405edb638ec.avif "Untransfected HEK293 — the experiment’s zero")

*The same two-round figure for the untransfected column, the plate's zero. Every trace in both
rounds stays inside ±0.05 — which is where the 0.045 noise floor and the four thresholds come from.*

**The fusion is expressed, reaches the plasma membrane, and gates Ca²⁺ in response to an Orco
agonist.** That conclusion rests on ΔF\_test and the shape, not on the inflated ΔF\_corr.

### The odorant rows

The three odorant conditions above 0.134 in the table (benzaldehyde, 2-heptanone, valeric acid) are
all step-shaped, frac 0.77–0.90, and all fail criterion 4. This part contains **no tuning receptor**
and has no odorant specificity to exercise, so those rows are the clearest evidence in the
experiment that the odorant working solutions differ physically from the assay buffer. They are
discussed at plate level in the collection's *Discussion* entry.

existing_entries.title: How far below the published reference this sits, and why
existing_entries.value:
### Magnitude

| | ΔF to 50 µM VUAA1 |
|---|---|
| this part, transient HEK293, n = 1 | **0.215** corrected · **0.119** ligand round alone |
| Zboray *et al.* (2023), selected stable clones, dox-induced | **1.24 – 4.62** |

**6–21× lower on the corrected value, 10–39× on the ligand round alone.** The most likely reason is
expression level, and it is not subtle: their lines are antibiotic-selected stable clones induced
with 1 µg/mL doxycycline for 48–72 h; this is a transient mixed population in which an unknown
fraction of cells carry the construct. The same plate supports that independently — only 2 of 11
Orco-containing columns responded to VUAA1 at all.

The 15 aa linker (vs their 8 aa) is a second candidate explanation that this experiment cannot
separate from the first. Resolving it needs both linkers on one plate at matched expression.

### Kinetics

Plateau at ~156 s here; Zboray *et al.* (2023) report maximum within 10 s using an **in-reader injector**. Our 50 µL
was added by hand with the plate out of the reader, so the measured onset includes removal,
pipetting and re-insertion. **The true channel kinetics are faster than this figure shows** and
156 s should not be quoted as a response time. An injector is the only way to measure it properly.

### Limitations

- **n = 1.** One well, one plate, one day.
- **The vehicle round of the reported well fell 9.6 %**, so ΔF_corr +0.215 is inflated by roughly
  45 %. See the *Characterisation* entry; the defensible number is ΔF_test +0.119.
- Cells detached progressively over the 2.5 h session on an uncoated plate. Use poly-D-lysine and
  keep time in assay buffer under ~40 min — this is also the most likely cause of the point above.
- Detector gain was not held constant across the session; the row reported here passed the gain QC,
  two other rows did not and were discarded.
- **Never blotted.** The RSET leader exists to answer "was the protein made?" and has not been used.
  See `BBa_262WP16P`.
- Ca²⁺ dependence was **not** re-demonstrated here. Zboray *et al.* (2023) established that the signal from this
  architecture requires extracellular Ca²⁺ by abolishing it in Ca²⁺-free and Ca²⁺-free + EGTA
  buffer. We inherited that and did not repeat it; a Ca²⁺-free row would make this collection's
  validation self-contained.

existing_entries.title: A 15-aa GS linker: when to use it, and what is actually known about this length
existing_entries.value:
### Use

Place in frame, with no stop codon, between two domains that must each fold and function
independently while staying physically tethered. Glycine gives backbone flexibility; serine keeps it
soluble. It encodes no structure and no epitope, and is not cleaved.

### Why three repeats

The length was chosen for the specific fusion in this collection: a ~50 kDa multi-domain calcium
indicator joined to a 7-TM membrane protein. Zboray *et al.* (2023) joined the same two proteins with a shorter
**8-aa** Gly₂SerGly₃SerGly linker. We lengthened it to 15 aa so neither folding process would
constrain the other; the reasoning is set out on `BBa_26E11Z80`.

**What this part's data does and does not support:** the fusion built with it is functional (ΔF_corr
+0.2148, ligand round +0.1186, to 50 µM VUAA1). It does **not** show that 15 aa is better than 8 aa,
or than any other length. Nobody has run the two side by side. Treat 15 aa as "a length that worked
once", not as an optimum; if the geometry matters to your fusion, build the series.

### Source

Fully synthetic — there is no source organism. The amino acid sequence is the standard
(Gly-Gly-Gly-Gly-Ser)×3 motif; at the DNA level the three repeats are written with **diversified
synonymous codons**, so the sequence contains no tandem repeat. That matters practically: tandem
repeats are a common cause of synthesis failure and of polymerase slippage during amplification.

### Characterisation status

Not characterised in isolation — a linker has no phenotype alone and there is no signal curve for
it. Its only functional evidence is that the fusion containing it works; see `BBa_26E11Z80`.

### Reference

1. Zboray K, Mohamed Mahmoud M, Pató A, *et al.* Stable cell lines expressing *Drosophila* odorant receptors for the detection of plant pathogen-related volatile organic compounds. *Sci Rep* **13**, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4

**This is a building block, not a device.** Or35a binds odorant but has no pore and cannot reach the
plasma membrane on its own: it requires the co-receptor Orco, which supplies both (`BBa_26LWIKBQ`,
or the reporter fusion `BBa_26E11Z80`). Expressed alone it stays in the ER.

### When to use this part rather than the module

Use **this CDS** when assembling Or35a into your own expression context — your own promoter, tag,
fluorescent marker or polycistronic design. Use **`BBa_26LLF3LM`** instead for a ready bicistronic unit with a
GCCACC Kozak and an IRES-mCherry expression marker already in place.

As supplied, this part needs a promoter, a Kozak (or an upstream in-frame fusion) and a polyA.

### Why codon-optimised

The reasoning is collection-wide and is documented in the collection documentation (*Drosophila odorant receptor calcium-reporter platform*): Zboray *et al.* (2023) used wild-type OR sequences, found
translation to be a likely bottleneck in HEK293, and recommended codon optimisation. Every receptor
CDS in this collection follows that recommendation.

| | |
|---|---|
| Organism | *Drosophila melanogaster* |
| Reference gene | FlyBase **FBgn0028946** |
| Reference transcript | FlyBase **FBtr0080781** |
| RefSeq protein | **NP_723916** |
| Encoded protein | **409 aa, identical to the FlyBase reference** — only the codons differ |
| How obtained | codon-optimised for human expression and **synthesised by GenScript**, delivered in an IP-free version of the pcDNA3.1(+) backbone |

*D. melanogaster* protein sequence, back-translated with human codon usage.

**Not characterised in isolation**, and it cannot meaningfully be — a tuning receptor alone produces
no signal, so there is no signal curve to show on this page. Functional testing was done on `BBa_26LLF3LM`
co-transfected with `BBa_26E11Z80`; the signal curves, the three ΔF values per compound, the
acceptance criteria and the controls are on that part's page, and what is known about Or35a from the

existing_entries.title: Why Or85b, and what is already known about it
existing_entries.value:
This module supplies one thing to the platform: **the ligand specificity of Or85b**. The pore, the
trafficking and the read-out all come from `BBa_26E11Z80`; the collection's *Design* entry covers
that split and the collection-wide choices (codon optimisation, the IRES-mCherry arrangement, the
Kozak, the absence of a promoter).

### Prior art for this receptor

**Positive precedent — one of only two receptors in the collection with a working mammalian
reference.** Zboray *et al.* (2023) obtained a responsive Or85b HEK293 line. Its reference ligand is **2-heptanone**,
EC₅₀ **68.9 µM**, chosen over the DoOR suggestion of butyl acetate. VUAA1-normalised responses
reported there, at 1 / 10 / 100 µM:

| ligand | 1 µM | 10 µM | 100 µM |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2-heptanone | 0.04 | 0.20 | 0.55 |
| 2-heptanol | 0.05 | 0.05 | 0.32 |
| α-funebrene | 0.10 | 0.00 | 0.26 |

Earlier work put the same EC₅₀ at 70 ± 20 µM in *Xenopus* oocytes (Nichols & Luetje 2010) and
45.6 µM (Misawa *et al.* 2010). Or85b was chosen for the collection precisely because this reference
curve exists: it is the receptor against which the platform can be checked quantitatively.

### What the odorant panel offered this receptor

**2-heptanone was on the plate, and it is this receptor's reference ligand** — Zboray *et al.* (2023) report
VUAA1-normalised 0.55 at 100 µM, EC₅₀ 68.9 µM. It is the only compound in the panel with a
quantitative published match to a receptor in this collection that survived the gain QC. It was
nevertheless dosed at 1:10,000 rather than by EC₅₀; see this part's *Discussion* entry.

The panel as a whole, and why it is weaker than it should be, is in the collection's *Design* entry.

### Source

The receptor coding sequence is `BBa_26DVVZIA` — FlyBase accession, protein length and synthesis route are on
that part's page. The module adds an EMCV IRES and mCherry (Shaner *et al.* 2004) around it; the
whole construct was synthesised by GenScript in an IP-free pcDNA3.1(+) backbone.

### Use

Co-transfect with **`BBa_26E11Z80`**. Neither part is a sensor alone. For Or85b in your own expression
context, use the bare CDS `BBa_26DVVZIA` instead.

mCherry from the IRES is the diagnostic that matters for this part specifically: red cells with no
calcium response localise the fault **downstream of transcription** — translation, folding or
trafficking — which is exactly the failure mode seen on this plate.

### Reference

Zboray K, Mohamed Mahmoud M, Pató A, *et al.* Stable cell lines expressing *Drosophila* odorant receptors for the detection of plant pathogen-related volatile organic compounds. *Sci Rep* **13**, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4

| compound                             | final conc. | ΔF\_blank | ΔF\_test | **ΔF\_corr**  | reading                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------- | --------- | -------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| VUAA1                                | 50 µM       | -0.0179   | +0.0065  | **+0.0243**   | below the 0.134 threshold — no response detected                                                                                        |
| 3-octanol                            | 1:10,000    | +0.0045   | +0.0257  | **+0.0212**   | below the 0.134 threshold — no response detected                                                                                        |
| benzaldehyde                         | 1:10,000    | +0.0158   | +0.0385  | **+0.0227**   | below the 0.134 threshold — no response detected                                                                                        |
| 2-heptanone                          | 1:10,000    | +0.0571   | +0.0508  | **-0.0063**   | below the 0.134 threshold — no response detected                                                                                        |
| valeric acid                         | 1:10,000    | -0.0127   | +0.2040  | **+0.2167**   | **passes all four criteria**, but frac 0.59 sits just inside the 0.60 bound — only marginally gradual (peak 48 s)                       |
| Control (buffer only)                | —           | -0.0602   | -0.0002  | **+0.0600**   | below the 0.134 threshold — no response detected                                                                                        |
| ethyl propionate · isopentyl acetate | 1:10,000    | —         | —        | not evaluable | gain changed between the baseline and response reads in those two rows; both discarded by the QC in the collection's *Experiment* entry |

*Both measurement rounds for this well, raw fluorescence expressed as (F − F₀)/F₀ against time after the 50 µL addition. **Left:** round 1, plain assay buffer — the vehicle control for every trace on the right. **Right:** round 2, the compound. The quoted ΔF\_corr is the right-hand peak minus the left-hand peak, so a trace that sags on the left inflates it.*

**Positive control for this column.** VUAA1 at 50 µM acts on Orco and does not require Or85b, so it
tests whether this well was expressing at all. It **failed**: ΔF\_corr +0.0243, below the 0.134 threshold. Every odorant reading above has to be read in that light.

Plate-level context — the buffer-only control row, the decomposition of every above-threshold
condition, and the full 6 × 12 matrix — is in the collection's *Characterisation* entry.![Two line charts for the Or85b well. In round 2 the valeric-acid trace rises to +0.20 and plateaus by 48 seconds while the other five stay below +0.06; round 1 is flat.](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/23c24124-86a4-4ac8-850e-2983c7e23464/364b85d809cdeb6f6da87d320e8b163e4f978e6ed7f87060ca3226ec20434393.avif "Or85b — both measurement rounds, six compounds")

existing_entries.title: What the experiment does and does not establish for Or85b
existing_entries.value:
**The published reference ligand was tested here and did not respond: 2-heptanone gave
ΔF_corr −0.0063** (ΔF_test +0.0508, ΔF_blank +0.0571).

**The dose cannot be stated, so this null cannot be interpreted.** Zboray *et al.* (2023) report EC₅₀ = 68.9 µM and
reach 0.55 only at 100 µM. Our odorant came from a supplied stock of unrecorded concentration,
diluted 10,000-fold by a convention taken from *Drosophila* experiments in which the animal samples
the vapour above the liquid rather than the liquid itself (collection *Experiment* entry). The molar
concentration delivered to these cells is therefore unknown, and it is not possible to say whether
this well was tested above, below or near the EC₅₀. **This null is uninformative about Or85b**, and
it is the clearest illustration in the collection of why an unrecorded stock concentration ruins an
otherwise well-controlled experiment.

Establishing the concentration and running a dose series bracketing 68.9 µM is the prerequisite for
any further claim about this receptor.

**Valeric acid is the one odorant condition on the entire plate that passes all four acceptance
criteria**: ΔF_corr +0.2167, ΔF_test +0.2040, ΔF_blank −0.0127, frac 0.59, peak 48 s. The vehicle
round was quiet.

The shape is the weak part of it. frac 0.59 means **59 % of the total rise was already present at
the first post-addition cycle** — it clears the 0.60 bound by 0.01. The curve shows a jump to +0.12
within the first 12 s and then a slower climb to +0.21 by 48 s. That is not the unambiguous
~156 s ramp seen for VUAA1 on the reporter fusion, and with a 12 s cycle this assay cannot resolve
whether the first segment is channel opening or a solution artefact. An injector and a shorter cycle
would settle it.

It is still not callable, for three reasons that have nothing to do with this well:

1. The buffer-only well in the Or35a column reached ΔF_corr +0.4486 with a cleaner shape and no
   ligand (collection *Characterisation*). At n = 1 this plate cannot resolve a +0.217 from its own
   false-positive rate.
2. VUAA1 gave +0.0243 in this column — the well failed its own positive control, so there is no
   evidence the receptor was at the membrane at all.
3. **Valeric acid is not a reported Or85b ligand.** No carboxylic acid appears anywhere in the
   responsive ligand set of Zboray *et al.* (2023), for any of their seven lines.

It is the single most interesting condition to repeat in the collection, and that is all it is.

### Replication status

**n = 1.** One well per condition, one plate, one day. Two further compounds (ethyl propionate,
isopentyl acetate) were lost to the gain fault documented in the collection's *Experiment* entry.
Nothing here constrains the receptor itself — only this construct, in this chassis, at these
concentrations, on this plate.

### Reference

Zboray K, Mohamed Mahmoud M, Pató A, *et al.* Stable cell lines expressing *Drosophila* odorant receptors for the detection of plant pathogen-related volatile organic compounds. *Sci Rep* **13**, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4

existing_entries.value:
### Endpoint microscopy

The fixed HEK293 image set contains **2 technical fields** labelled Or35a+ORCO, with **200 eligible DAPI objects**. At the blank-derived p99 cutoff, RED-positive objects were **28/200 (14.0%)**, GREEN-positive **11/200 (5.5%)**, and both-positive **8/200 (4.0%)**. Eligible objects represented 10.2% of DAPI foreground.

These are counts around resolvable nuclear objects, not whole-culture transfection efficiency or viability. The images were acquired around 44–48 h after transfection, before G418 selection, after 2% PFA fixation and DAPI staining without recorded permeabilization. Field counts are technical sampling, not biological replication. The images do not establish plasma-membrane localization, and their batch relationship to P2 is unresolved.

The first numbered field is shown to make the endpoint readout inspectable without selecting the brightest field. Brightfield and DAPI provide cellular context; the GREEN and RED channels ask whether localized fluorescence accompanies the reporter fusion and independent mCherry marker.

![Or35a+ORCO field 01, brightfield and separate BLUE/GREEN/RED channels](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/6ffc966fa86bfd81411e389726871a464f984083a10d607260d70e7be3ad53ee.avif)

*Or35a+ORCO, field 01, fixed-cell image panel. Display windows are BLUE 0–255, GREEN 0–120 and RED 0–180 digital values; brightfield retains exported levels. These display adjustments are not the quantitative input. The analysis uses the original channel TIFFs and the same blank-derived criteria across conditions. Compare the [untransfected field 01](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/aerosense-assets-20261017/d7e6a0850fe4-field-01-panel.webp); the original 100 µm scale bars remain in the channel panels.*

| Blank-score cutoff | RED-positive objects | GREEN-positive objects |
|---|---:|---:|
| p95 | 70/200 (35.0%) | 27/200 (13.5%) |
| p99 | 28/200 (14.0%) | 11/200 (5.5%) |
| p99.5 | 23/200 (11.5%) | 7/200 (3.5%) |

*Counts across all available fields for this condition. p95, p99 and p99.5 are alternative blank-score cutoffs, not confidence levels or independent measurements. The denominator is unchanged across cutoffs.*

Both channels retain positive objects at p99.5, but the counts decrease from p99: RED 28 to 23 and GREEN 11 to 7. Eight objects are dual-positive at p99. This endpoint evidence should be considered alongside the unusually large buffer-only P2 value, rather than used to resolve that later assay effect.

### Test 1: paired-round fluorescence measurements

**Assay labels.** “Round 1” and “round 2” in the older plot are the buffer and test stages of **Test 1**, not separate tests. Its R/B/D table values are dimensionless (×100 gives percentage points). The later **[Test 2 characterization](#odor-2026-10-21)** below uses the same within-F1 minus within-F0 calculation as the wiki, with S in percentage points.

One plate, one well per condition–stimulus combination; raw export headers span **10–11 October 2026**. R = ΔFtest − ΔFblank; B subtracts the same-condition buffer-only well; D additionally subtracts the same-stimulus untransfected-minus-buffer contrast. Full equations, denominators, provenance and exclusions are in [the collection](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156).

existing_entries.value:
**This column is simultaneously the collection's one clean VUAA1 response in a tuning-receptor
well and its worst false positive. Both readings come from the same two wells and must be reported
together.**

**The good result.** VUAA1 gave ΔF_corr +0.1373 with ΔF_test +0.1776, ΔF_blank +0.0403 and frac 0.49

is only marginally gradual. Only two of the eleven Orco-containing columns responded
to the positive control at all, and this is one of them, so the construct was expressed here. That

existing_entries.title: Orco: inverted topology, obligate partnership, and its own pharmacology
existing_entries.value:
Three properties of Orco determine the shape of this entire collection. They are recorded here
because they are properties of **this molecule**; the other part pages refer to them rather than
restating them.

### 1. Inverted membrane topology

Orco is a 7-TM protein, but **not** a GPCR, and its topology is **inverted** relative to one: the
**N-terminus is intracellular**. This single fact is why calcium indicators in this architecture are
fused to the N-terminus rather than the C-terminus — see `BBa_26E11Z80`. The wrong way round puts
the indicator in 2 mM extracellular Ca²⁺, saturated, reporting nothing.

### 2. Obligate partner, and chaperone

Orco binds **no odorant**. It forms the heteromeric ligand-gated cation channel with any tuning
receptor, supplies the pore, and chaperones that receptor to the plasma membrane. Without Orco,
tuning receptors remain in the ER. Any construct in this collection expressed without Orco present
will produce no signal, for trafficking reasons before pharmacological ones.

The channel is a non-selective cation channel that conducts Ca²⁺, and the fluorescence signal in
GCaMP-based assays comes from **extracellular** Ca²⁺ entering through this pore. Zboray *et al.* (2023) established
this by abolishing the response in Ca²⁺-free buffer and in Ca²⁺-free buffer containing EGTA — which
is why the assay buffer in this collection contains 2 mM CaCl₂.

### 3. Its own agonist: VUAA1

**VUAA1 opens Orco-containing channels directly, bypassing the tuning receptor** (Jones *et al.*,
2011). That makes it the positive control for the whole platform and the reason every experiment
here includes a VUAA1 row: **if VUAA1 gives no response, the fault is in expression or read-out, not
in the odorant or the tuning receptor.** In this experiment that control is what showed 9 of 11
Orco-containing wells were not in a usable state — see the collection's *Discussion* entry.

### Design notes

- **Codon-optimised for human expression.** Zboray *et al.* (2023) codon-optimised Orco too, while leaving their
  tuning receptors wild-type.
- **Consider an inducible promoter for a stable line.** Constitutive Orco expression has been
  reported to reduce long-term viability (Corcoran *et al.*, as cited in Zboray *et al.* (2023)), which is why that
  study placed its Orco fusion under a doxycycline-inducible promoter. This part carries no
  promoter, so the choice is the host vector's. Zboray *et al.* (2023) also note they could not reproduce that
  toxicity for their own Or10a, Or49b and Or71a lines over 60 days.

### Source

| | |
|---|---|
| Organism | *Drosophila melanogaster* |
| Reference gene / transcript | FlyBase **FBgn0037324** / **FBtr0078794** |
| RefSeq protein | **NP_524235** |
| Encoded protein | **486 aa, identical to the FlyBase reference** — only the codons differ |
| How obtained | codon-optimised for human expression, **synthesised by GenScript**, delivered in an IP-free pcDNA3.1(+) backbone |

Not cloned from flies, not evolved, not computationally designed.

### Characterisation status

Not characterised in isolation — Orco alone is not the useful unit here, and there is no signal
curve for this part on its own. It was tested as part of `BBa_26E11Z80`, which gave ΔF_corr +0.2148
(ligand round +0.1186) to 50 µM VUAA1 in transiently transfected HEK293 with no tuning receptor
present. The curves, the decomposition and the limitations are on that part's page.

### References

1. Zboray K, Mohamed Mahmoud M, Pató A, *et al.* Stable cell lines expressing *Drosophila* odorant receptors for the detection of plant pathogen-related volatile organic compounds. *Sci Rep* **13**, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4
2. Jones PL, Pask GM, Rinker DC, Zwiebel LJ. Functional agonism of insect odorant receptor ion channels. *PNAS* **108**, 8821–8825 (2011).

Use **this CDS** when assembling Or59b into your own expression context — your own promoter, tag,
fluorescent marker or polycistronic design. Use **`BBa_26Y7CI2H`** instead for a ready bicistronic unit with a
GCCACC Kozak and an IRES-mCherry expression marker already in place.

translation to be a likely bottleneck in HEK293, and recommended codon optimisation. Every receptor

existing_entries.title: GCaMP6f as a read-out module: why the fast variant, and two properties that bite on a plate reader
existing_entries.value:
### How it works

Ca²⁺ binds calmodulin, calmodulin engages the M13 peptide, and the resulting conformational change
raises the quantum yield of the circularly permuted EGFP between them. The read-out is a
**fluorescence intensity change at one wavelength**, not a ratio — which is what makes the
within-well, two-round correction used throughout this collection necessary rather than optional.

### Why the "f" variant

Of the GCaMP6 family (Chen *et al.*, 2013), **6f is the fast variant**: lower peak amplitude than
6s, faster rise and decay. An insect OR channel opens in milliseconds, so the indicator should not
be the slow step. The cost is sensitivity, and that cost is visible in our data — see
`BBa_26E11Z80`.

### Two practical properties that affect how it is used

1. **It is dim at resting Ca²⁺.** On a plate reader the detector gain must be set so the *baseline*
   sits low in the range — in our hands ~10–15 % of full scale, not the ~90 % one would use for a
   bright constitutive reporter — or the response saturates. Full scale on our instrument was
   260,000 RFU with enhanced dynamic range off.
2. **The cpEGFP chromophore is pH-sensitive**, pKa ≈ 7.1–7.2, close to intracellular pH. A working
   solution whose pH differs slightly from the assay buffer will shift fluorescence with no Ca²⁺
   involved. This is a live concern in our own dataset and is discussed at plate level in the collection documentation (*Drosophila odorant receptor calcium-reporter platform*).

A third property showed up in practice and is worth stating: **a bright GCaMP well can lose baseline
over a long session.** The brightest well on our plate fell 9.6 % during a buffer-only round, which
the within-well correction then converted into an inflated response. Keep sessions short and check
the vehicle round.

### Use in this collection

Fused to the **N-terminus of Orco** (`BBa_26E11Z80`) so the indicator sits at the mouth of the
channel it reports on rather than free in the cytosol. It works equally as a cytosolic Ca²⁺ reporter
or fused to another target.

### Source

Derived from **Addgene #40755**. The indicator itself was developed and characterised by Chen
*et al.* (2013); this part is that coding region, not a redesign of it. Supplied as part of a
GenScript-synthesised fragment.

### Characterisation status

Not characterised in isolation, so there is no signal curve for this part alone. In the fusion it
gave ΔF_corr +0.2148 (ligand round +0.1186) to 50 µM VUAA1 — which shows it folds and reports after
being tethered to a membrane protein through a 15 aa linker. No cytosolic-only comparison was run,
so the cost of the tethering is unmeasured.

### References

1. Chen T-W, Wardill TJ, Sun Y, *et al.* Ultrasensitive fluorescent proteins for imaging neuronal activity. *Nature* **499**, 295–300 (2013).
2. Zboray K, Mohamed Mahmoud M, Pató A, *et al.* Stable cell lines expressing *Drosophila* odorant receptors for the detection of plant pathogen-related volatile organic compounds. *Sci Rep* **13**, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4

| valeric acid                         | 1:10,000    | +0.0414   | +0.0243  | **-0.0170**   | below the 0.134 threshold — no response detected                                                                                        |

| VUAA1                                | 50 µM       | +0.0102   | -0.0447  | **-0.0549**   | below the 0.134 threshold — no response detected                                                                                                                                                     |
| 3-octanol                            | 1:10,000    | -0.0032   | +0.0929  | **+0.0961**   | below the 0.134 threshold — no response detected                                                                                                                                                     |

| valeric acid                         | 1:10,000    | +0.0395   | +0.0119  | **-0.0276**   | below the 0.134 threshold — no response detected                                                                                                                                                     |

**Correction to an earlier reading of this data.** The 2-heptanone well in this column reports
ΔF_corr +0.1835, which at first looked like the largest gradual odorant signal in the collection and
was written up as the condition most worth repeating. Decomposing the two rounds shows that is
wrong:

| | value |
|---|---|
| ΔF_blank (round 1, plain buffer) | **−0.1637** |
| ΔF_test (round 2, 2-heptanone) | **+0.0198** |
| ΔF_corr | +0.1835 |

**The ligand round barely moved.** The reported value is almost entirely the vehicle round losing
16 % of its baseline, which the subtraction turns into a positive number. 89 % of +0.1835 is that
movement. It fails criteria 2 and 3 (see the collection's *Characterisation* entry) and **is not a
candidate response at all.**

Everything else in this column is below threshold, and VUAA1 gave −0.0549, so the well also failed
its own positive control. This plate therefore says nothing about Or7a — it adds one failed positive
control and one artefact.

The useful observation is a negative one for the method: a well that loses baseline during the
vehicle round will manufacture a convincing-looking response. That is why every table in this
collection reports all three of ΔF_blank, ΔF_test and ΔF_corr.

### Replication status

**n = 1.** One well per condition, one plate, one day. Two further compounds (ethyl propionate,
isopentyl acetate) were lost to the gain fault documented in the collection's *Experiment* entry.
Nothing here constrains the receptor itself — only this construct, in this chassis, at these
concentrations, on this plate.
